title: SCE authoring profile (wire schema v1)
description: What a specification owner configures about how documents are authored for them: a file beside the specification, read by `sce-codegen check --profile`, `generate --profile` and `orchestrate --profile` and by the authoring MCP, and pinned by an acceptance record as part of what a design was authored from. It is data, never code, and names no subject matter. Every setting belongs to ONE class, fixed by this schema and not by the file: enforced (a draft that breaks it is refused), reported (a departure is listed and the owner decides), or guidance (handed to the author, checked by nothing). Version 1 holds one enforced setting. A build that meets a setting it does not know refuses the whole profile, so a profile written for a newer tool is never half applied. Authoritative reader is sce-build/src/authoring_profile.rs. The stability status of this surface lives in this header alone — see SCE_WIRE_CONTRACTS.md.

record.description: Names the kind of file, so a JSON document of another kind is refused before its settings are read.

v.description: Schema version. Bumped only on a breaking shape change; a setting is added without a bump.

name.description: A label a report may print. Not a setting: it configures nothing, and it is part of the file's bytes like every other character, so renaming a profile is a new profile to an acceptance record.

interface.description: ENFORCED. `closed`: every statechart declares `sce:interface="closed"`, so it takes and sends only the events its imported event-schemas declare (docs/SCE_ACCEPTED_SUBSET.md §2.16) and the boundary the owner accepted is the one it is held to. A statechart that does not is refused as `profile/interface-not-closed`. Absent: the interface is not constrained, and a statechart that leaves it open is the owner's choice. It applies to statecharts alone; a forge document has no such interface and is not judged.
